statement: RTS Link passenger service target is February 2027 (moved from January 2027 on 2026-10-02); exact date and fares not yet announced
rationale: Joint MY-SG statement reported by Malay Mail; reason given: third-party safety certification and approvals
used_in: Scenario A timing; Stage 5 freeze deadline
how_tested: Re-check monthly until date announced; freeze ridership range before announced date

statement: RTS Link design capacity is 10000 passengers per hour per direction
rationale: Consistent across MRT Corp; LTA and MOT SG references
used_in: Bukit Chagar stress test upper bound on peak flow
how_tested: Probe SRC-003 for term; consistency check vs headway x train capacity (=10000)

statement: MRT Corp expects about 40000 daily riders on opening
rationale: Opening-period forecast; method not published
how_tested: Term 40,000 confirmed on the MRT Corp page by Actions probe 2026-11-04; compared with observed ridership after opening (V9)

statement: The 35% x 350,000 = 122,500/day figure is a mature, capacity-constrained upper case, not an opening-year forecast
rationale: Under A-010 peaking it loads the peak direction to 61-123% of design capacity (results/stage1/rts_ridership_bounds.json)
how_tested: Arithmetic reproducible from pipeline/analysis/rts_ridership_bounds.py

statement: RTS train capacity ~600 passengers (4-car) and peak headway ~3.6 min
rationale: Enthusiast/press figures; product equals the official 10000 pphpd
how_tested: Replace with operator figures when published

statement: RTS operating hours 06:00-24:00 daily
rationale: Reported expectation; minister declined 24-hour service
how_tested: Replace with announced hours

statement: RTS in-vehicle time Bukit Chagar-Woodlands North
rationale: Reported ~5 min; a test ride was reported at ~6 min
how_tested: Replace with published timetable

statement: Co-located CIQ: travelers clear both countries' border controls at the departure station only
rationale: Repeated in official statements
used_in: Bukit Chagar stress test (processing at departure)
how_tested: Site check after opening (SC-6)

statement: Malaysian ICQ at Bukit Chagar has ~100 e-gate lanes; per-traveler processing time unknown (7 s claim is unverified)
rationale: Single press report; processing rate not official
how_tested: Site check SC-6; seek official ICQ capacity

statement: Peak-direction peak-hour flow as a share of two-way daily ridership
rationale: Commuter peak hour 8-12% of daily two-way trips; tidal split 60/40 to 80/20 for cross-border work trips
how_tested: Update from observed hourly gate counts after opening

statement: Stage 1 planning bounds for 2027 daily RTS ridership (NOT a forecast)
rationale: Low = slow ramp-up; base = official; high = 2x official; mature upper case = 122500
how_tested: Superseded by the frozen Stage 5 prediction range

statement: E-ART line capacity per corridor
rationale: Reports conflict: typical ART 3000-5000; 4800 at 20 tph x 240; 5000-12000 by car count; 10000 design claim. 12000 treated as out of range until a vehicle spec is published
how_tested: Replace with procurement/vehicle spec when published

statement: Reported E-ART corridor lengths: Tebrau 14 km, Iskandar Puteri 14.78 km (Skudai 18.8 km, out of scope)
rationale: Reported by the state exco in May 2024 (SRC-045, SRC-046 corroborate SRC-021); search snippets only; the Actions probe did not find 14.78/18.8 on the theSun page. Figures may predate the 2026 revised proposal (SRC-043)
used_in: Stage 2 hypotheses must be checked against these lengths (+/-15%)
how_tested: Stage 2: each hypothesis length compared with the reported length (+/-15%), results/stage2/option_comparison.csv

statement: E-ART alignments, station locations, depots and vehicle spec are unpublished; station counts conflict (32, 35, 39). Reported mid-2026: general alignment agreed between consortium and state, >half of station sites set, but not published
rationale: No official alignment drawing located
used_in: All Stage 2 geometry is labeled concept
how_tested: Re-searched 2026-11-04 (Stage 2): no published alignment, no letter of acceptance. Re-search before Stage 6

statement: E-ART will not be operating in 2027; earliest plausible opening is ~2030-2031
rationale: 4-year build from letter of acceptance; LOA not confirmed issued as of the latest sources
used_in: Framing: B and C are future-network concepts evaluated on 2027 land use
how_tested: Track LOA/award news; 2026-11-04: still letter of intent only (SRC-015, SRC-043)

statement: Scenarios B and C use 2027 population and destinations (no land-use forecast)
rationale: No published small-area land-use forecast; avoids inventing growth
how_tested: State as limitation

statement: Access metric departure window weekday 07:00-08:00 (median travel time); evening 17:30-18:30 for Bukit Chagar dispersal
rationale: Standard practice for cumulative-opportunity access
how_tested: Sensitivity with other windows

statement: Walking speed
rationale: r5py default 3.6; low case reflects heat and crossings
how_tested: Compare with timed walks (SC-2)

statement: myBAS Johor GTFS represents existing BAS.MY Johor Bahru bus service (21 routes; service 2026-10-05 to 2027-02-02); KTMB GTFS covers rail (calendar ends 2026-11-18, refreshed daily)
rationale: Official open feeds
how_tested: S0 PASS 2026-11-04 (feed current); V1 validator in Stage 5; SC-3 on-street check; V3a vehicle positions collected from 2026-11-04 on branch vp-data

statement: Open GTFS contains only BAS.MY (bus) and KTMB (rail) for Johor; cross-border and private operators (e.g. Causeway Link) are absent
rationale: agency.txt of the 2026-11-04 myBAS feed lists one agency
how_tested: Confirmed from agency.txt; size of the gap via SC-3

statement: Bukit Chagar is the planned main interchange between RTS Link and E-ART
rationale: Repeated in official statements

statement: Claim: Tebrau is the priority because ~75% of vehicles entering/leaving JB use that route (official statement, data source not given)
rationale: Treated as a CLAIM TO TEST; not used as a model input
how_tested: V10 using free count data only (owner declined paid RTVM 2026-11-04); reported UNTESTED if no free counts are found

statement: Experts (Oct 2026) propose Skudai-Tampoi-Larkin and Tebrau-Pandan as the two priority corridors; Iskandar Puteri was not named
rationale: Expert opinion; not a government decision
how_tested: Owner decision 2026-11-04: keep Scenario C = Iskandar Puteri; Skudai appears only as a sensitivity note

statement: Woodlands Checkpoint averaged 327,000 travelers/day in 2024 (269,000 in 2023)
rationale: ICA official

statement: Population base: DOSM Census 2020 at the finest published geography; disaggregation to a grid method TBD (building footprints or GHSL)
rationale: Finest confirmed public geography is parliament/state seat
how_tested: Check against DOSM totals (sum-preserving)

statement: Elevated guideway hypotheses follow existing road reserves; routing on the OSM road graph prefers named spine roads (x0.3), then trunk/primary, and avoids expressways unless the option is about them (x4)
rationale: Elevated ART/LRT in Malaysia is typically built over road medians to limit land take; the factors only shape the hypothesis and are not engineering
how_tested: Sensitivity: options with and without preferred roads; compare with any official alignment when published

statement: Station catchment = 800 m street-network walk
rationale: Common 10-minute walk standard; matches V2 and V10 indicator 1
how_tested: Stage 3 recomputes catchments in R5 at 3.0/3.6/4.5 km/h

statement: Station spacing 1.0-1.5 km, placed by maximizing unique building floor-area proxy (footprint area x building:levels where tagged, else x1) within the 800 m walk; interchange and terminus stations forced
rationale: Brief asks for ~1-1.5 km spacing by walk-catchment logic; floor-area proxy is the only consistent activity measure in OSM before Stage 3 population disaggregation
how_tested: Stage 3 re-scores with DOSM-based residents and jobs proxies; spacing sensitivity in run times

statement: Building-to-building clear width needed: line 16/20/25 m; elevated station 24/30/36 m (low/base/high). Below base = pinch point; below low = high severity
rationale: Double-track viaduct deck ~9-10 m plus ~5 m clearance to facades each side; side-platform station box ~20-25 m wide. Not from a vehicle spec (unpublished)
how_tested: Replace with project cross-sections if published; no field check possible (SC-4 substitute)

statement: Minimum horizontal curve radius screens: 50 m (rubber-tired ART / APM) and 100 m (light rail)
rationale: Technology not confirmed (A-035), so both screens are reported
how_tested: Replace with vehicle spec

statement: Maximum sustained grade screens: 5% (steel-wheel rail) and 8% (rubber-tired)
rationale: Ground grade from a DSM over 200 m after 250 m median smoothing; an elevated guideway can smooth ground grades, so this is a screen only
how_tested: Replace with a DTM or project profile if published

statement: Flood screen: JRC RP100 river-flood depth >0, or DSM elevation <=5 m within 150 m of a mapped waterway or the coastline (low-lying proxy). News reports are leads only
rationale: JB flooding is mostly flash (pluvial) and tidal, which no free layer captures; this is coarse
how_tested: No local observation possible (SC-5 substitute); compare with official hotspot lists if found

statement: Depot land screen: OSM landuse greenfield/brownfield/grass/meadow/farmland/orchard/plantation or natural scrub/grassland, >=5 ha (base 8 ha; LRT-scale 15 ha), <=1.5 km from the line, building cover <=5%. Land ownership is unknown
rationale: Small ART depots ~5-8 ha; LRT depots 15+ ha. OSM does not record government land, so candidates are inferred, not available
how_tested: Check against state land data if published; depots are reportedly still being agreed (SRC-043)

statement: Bus interchange measure: distinct BAS.MY GTFS routes with a stop within 400 m network walk of a station; KTM within 800 m
rationale: Shorter transfer walk than the station catchment
how_tested: Stage 3 timetable-based transfer times

statement: E-ART technology is not confirmed: described as elevated autonomous rapid transit (rubber-tired) by government, but as a rail system in a company filing; an LRT-style APM was reported possible (June 2026)
rationale: Conflicting reports; no vehicle spec
used_in: Curve and grade screens use both technologies; capacity range A-012 unchanged
how_tested: Track procurement news

statement: The reported 14.78 km Iskandar Puteri length is shorter than any road-reserve route from Bukit Chagar to Kota Iskandar or Puteri Harbour computed in Stage 2; the official line probably does not run Bukit Chagar to the Iskandar Puteri administrative center as a single line
rationale: See results/stage2/option_comparison.csv (IP options); to be confirmed by the full-area run
how_tested: Owner decision at the end of Stage 2
